newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate panel OKs lease-debt reform measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate panel OKs lease-debt reform measure.

text.p: A California legislative panel on Wednesday approved a controversial bill that would force local governments to seek voter approval for certain lease-backed debt issues.
The state Senate's Local Government Committee approved Senate Bill 147 with amendments on a vote of 4-to-1. The bill now advanced to the Senate Education Committee.
The bill's author, Senator Ruben Ayala, accused the committee of "watering down" the original measure, and said he may drop the bill altogether because of the changes.
When introduced in January, Ayala's bill called for majority voter approval of all forms of certificate of participation debt.

As amended Wednesday, Senate Bill 147 would require local governments to obtain majority voter approval before issuing medium- to long-term certificates of participation (COPs) backed by developer fee revenues.
The bill still requires local governments issuing COPs to inform their communities about the proposed borrowings by holding public hearings.
The current version of Senate Bill 147 does not impact local agencies' tax, revenue and grant anticipation notes, traditional revenue bonds, and conduit financings.
Supporters of the measure argued that the public should have more control over COPs because this form of debt can drain local government finances.
